subject: Pricing & context-length follow-up: token volumes and target $/1M
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:02:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & context-length profiling (recap + next steps)

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the immediate asks we discussed so we can get pricing into a ballpark for your finance team. High-level notes: we heard that Acme's use case is a customer support + summarization pipeline that sometimes needs long context for enterprise tickets.

Recap from call: 
- Typical workload: asynchronous support workflows + nightly batch summarization + live agent assist.
- Avg prompt tokens (per request): ~1.2k tokens (includes ticket context + prompt template).
- Avg completion tokens: ~600 tokens (summaries + suggested responses).
- Daily request volume: ~15k API calls/day (spiky during business hours).
- Context length needs: ~70% use <=8k, ~25% need 32k, ~5% need 128k for large case histories.

As discussed, to price accurately we need to align on two things: (1) target $/1M tokens you're budgeting for, and (2) whether you prefer on-demand pricing vs a committed monthly spend (committed gives significant unit discounts).

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm the numbers above or share a sample token profile (CSV) from your logs? (we can ingest to produce a cost projection)
2) What is your target unit economics (e.g., $X per 1M tokens)? You mentioned a ~ $3/1M target on the call — confirm if that's illustrative or a hard constraint.
3) Are you open to a 6–12 month committed tier if we can meet your target $/1M?

I've attached a lightweight template (acme_token_profile.csv) you can paste numbers into; if easier you can send raw logs and we'll run a short profiling pass. I'll also attach our latest pricing tier PDF for transparency.

Proposed evaluation plan (if you want):
- Send token profile -> we return projected monthly token counts split by context bucket (8k/32k/128k) and an expected monthly bill on both on-demand and 6/mo commit pricing.
- Run a pilot (approx. 1–2 weeks) using Redwood hosted endpoint with limited credits to validate latency and cost.

Thanks — aim to get a draft pricing figure to you by EOD tomorrow after I have the token profile.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: acme_token_profile.csv, redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf

Thanks Marissa — appreciation for the clear recap. Numbers below are approximate but representative. I'll attach a quick export as well.

Confirming: 
- Avg prompt tokens: 1,150–1,300 (1.2k is right)
- Avg completion tokens: ~550–650 (use 600 avg)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & context-length profiling (recap + next steps)

Alex — great, thanks for the export. I ran a quick profile and here's an initial, conservative projection and recommended commercial options. These are ballpark—I'll finalize after we ingest the full CSV.

Projected monthly tokens (based on 15k calls/day and your distributions):
- 8k bucket (70%): ~240M tokens/month
- 32k bucket (25%): ~120M tokens/month (higher tokens per call driven by long context)
- 128k bucket (5%): ~36M tokens/month (batch/very long threads)
- Total: ~396M tokens/month

Unit pricing options (illustrative):
- On-demand: $5.00 per 1M tokens (no commit) -> ~$1,980/month
  (note: this on-demand price is illustrative and we can show exact math per token type; on-demand for long contexts includes extra compute premium)
- 6-month commit (monthly average): $3.50 per 1M tokens -> ~$1,386/month
- 12-month commit / larger commitment: $2.50 per 1M tokens -> ~$990/month

I want to call out two important items for finance: 
1) Context length drives GPU memory & throughput deltas. 32k and 128k calls cost disproportionately more due to KV cache memory and extra attention compute; we price by tokens but with a context-premium baked into the higher context buckets.
2) Committed spend smooths variability and lets us allocate Dedicated capacity, which reduces unit costs and improves latency predictability.

Given your target ~$2.5–$3.5/1M: the 6–12 month committed options get into that range. If finance needs $15k/month as the starting budget, that covers smaller initial pilot capacity; the committed discounts we quoted above require a commitment to a minimum monthly spend — we should align on an exact committed volume number.

Next steps I propose: 
- I will run the full CSV through our cost profiler and return a per-bucket bill with expected monthly totals and a 6/12 month committed pricing schedule (by EOD today).
- If the committed tiers look good, we can draft a mutual action plan and an initial SOW + purchase order path for procurement.

If acceptable, I'd also schedule a brief call with Jordan (cc'd) to walk the procurement team/state the SLA expectations and options for committed discounts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf

Marissa
